newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy sees improved fiscal second half.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy sees improved fiscal second half.

text.p: Consumer electronics retailer Best Buy Co Inc, reporting lower fiscal second quarter earnings, said on Wednesday it expects improved results in the second half.
"We continue to make progress on the initiatives announced earlier this year," Richard Schulze, chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

"We believe these initiatives and strong consumer preference for our store presentation should result in improved operating results for the second half of fiscal 1997, as compared to the prior year," he said.

Earnings for the second quarter were $3.7 million, or $0.09 per share, compared to $5.7 million, or $0.13 per share, in the year-ago quarter. Revenues were $1.77 billion, up 24 percent from the same quarter last year.

"Our comparable-store sales results have benefited from an enhanced major appliance assortment and an increased emphasis on selling extended service plans," Schulze said. "Both initiatives helped to mitigate the effects of a continued promotional environment for personal computers and industry-wide softness in consumer electronics."
Gross profit margins were 14.1 percent in the second quarter, compared to 13.7 percent a year ago.

"Revenues, margin and operating income were adversely impacted as compared to last year's second quarter by soft sales of air conditioners due to the relatively mild summer experienced throughout much of the nation," the company said.
Selling, general and administrative expenses were 13 percent of sales for the quarter, compared to 12.3 percent a year ago.
"The increase in the expense ratio is mainly the result of the fixed expenses associated with new stores and distribution facilities opened in the past 12 months," the company said.

It said it intends to open 10 new stores during its third quarter. The expansion will include entry into the Tampa, Fla., market with four stores, as well as one store in the new market of Memphis, Tenn.
